sections.title: Basic Concept
sections.content: In Direction Sense, a person's direction, distance, and final position are determined.  The main directions are North, South, East, and West. Questions also include left and right turns. The objective is to understand where the person reached from start to finish and which direction they are facing.

sections.title: Main Directions and Turns
sections.content: If a person is facing North, turning right will make them face East, and turning left will make them face West. If facing South, right will be West and left will be East. Always determine left and right according to the current facing direction.

sections.title: Calculation of Distance
sections.content: Total distance means the entire distance covered by the person; simply add all the segments together. Example: Walking 5 km North and 3 km East makes the total distance 8 km.

sections.title: Shortest Distance
sections.content: To find the straight-line distance between the starting and ending points, use Pythagorean triplets.  If a person goes 3 km North and 4 km East, the shortest distance will be 5 km (the 3-4-5 rule).

sections.title: Final Facing Direction
sections.content: Apply each turn given in the question sequentially. The direction the person is looking at the end will be the final facing direction.

sections.title: Important Triplets
sections.content: Remember Pythagorean triplets like 3-4-5 and 5-12-13. This helps in calculating the Shortest Distance quickly.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Assuming left-right based only on the North direction. 2. Confusion between total distance and shortest distance. 3. Forgetting the final facing direction.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Direction, distance, and final position are the key points in Direction Sense. Drawing a diagram makes solving questions much easier.

tricks.title: Always assume North is upwards
tricks.explanation: On paper, draw North pointing up, South down, East right, and West left.
tricks.example: Turning right from North will lead to East.

tricks.title: Determine Left-Right from Current Direction
tricks.explanation: Turns are always counted relative to the current facing direction.
tricks.example: If facing East, a left turn will point North.

tricks.title: Add up Total Distance
tricks.example: 4 km North + 6 km South = 10 km total distance traveled.

tricks.title: Triplets for Shortest Distance
tricks.example: 3 km North and 4 km East = 5 km straight-line distance.

tricks.title: Subtract Opposite Directions
tricks.explanation: North and South are opposites; East and West are opposites.
tricks.example: 6 km North and 2 km South = remaining 4 km North.

tricks.title: Make a Chart for Final Direction
tricks.explanation: Right from North is East, right from East is South, right from South is West.
tricks.example: Turning right twice takes you from North to South.

tricks.title: Solve in 2-3 Steps
tricks.explanation: First calculate the net North-South movement, then East-West.

tricks.title: Don't Forget to Draw a Diagram
tricks.explanation: A small sketch makes the question clear.
tricks.example: In a question with three turns, draw lines and keep changing the direction.

tricks.title: Facing Direction Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Right turn = Clockwise, Left turn = Anti-clockwise. [Image illustrating clockwise and anti-clockwise directions for left and right turns]
tricks.example: One Right turn from North = East.

tricks.title: Think Net Movement
tricks.explanation: Instead of individual movements, think about the final position.
tricks.example: 5 North and 5 South = Return to the starting point.
